title: How College Park Rentals and UMD Pollen Load Your Air Ducts
headline: High occupancy, campus trees, and why Route 1 houses stay dusty between tenants
description: College Park, MD houses and apartments turn over fast around UMD. Learn why neglected filters, packed dryer vents, and pollen load the ducts, and when to clean them.

sections.heading: College Park indoor air is a occupancy problem
paragraphs: Houses off Route 1 and apartments near campus often hold more people than a suburban colonial. Filters go months without a change. Dryers run every day. Ducts that were never cleaned between leases keep recirculating whatever the last group left behind — dust, pollen from the campus canopy, cooking residue, pet dander.
Maryland humidity still sits in cool trunks. The first hot week of the semester is when the smell shows up.

sections.heading: The dryer vent is the fire and humidity problem
paragraphs: Student and rental units pack lint faster than owner-occupied houses. A clogged cap dumps heat and moisture back into the laundry. That moisture feeds whatever is already in the ducts.
Owners and managers should start with [air duct cleaning in College Park, MD](/locations/college-park) at turnover, not after the next complaint.

sections.heading: Typical signs in a College Park rental
listItems: Dust returning days after a make-ready clean.
Musty air when the AC starts in August.
A dryer that needs two cycles and a hot closet.

sections.heading: Bethesda dispatch — no fake Route 1 shop
paragraphs: College Park is served from our [Bethesda](/locations/bethesda) office. [Silver Spring](/locations/silver-spring) and [Washington, DC](/locations/washington-dc) are nearby pages.
Book on the [College Park location page](/locations/college-park). Pair [dryer vent cleaning](/dryer-vent-cleaning) with ducts at each long-term move-out.
listItems: Clean ducts at turnover on high-occupancy houses, not only every five years.
Clear dryer vents about once a year or at move-out.
Change filters on a schedule the tenants will actually follow — or the manager will.

faq.q: Do you work for College Park landlords?
faq.a: Yes. Turnover cleanings and packed dryer vents are a normal job. We document with before-and-after photos.

faq.q: Does campus pollen really reach indoor ducts?
faq.a: Yes. Returns pull outdoor air. UMD’s tree canopy is not decorative in May. The load sits in the trunks until they are cleaned.
